blocks.content: Tool Definition is the engineering practice used to describe callable capabilities to a model.

Describe callable capabilities to a model. In production, the hard part is not a single successful demo; it is building a contract that remains observable, secure, testable, and predictable under real traffic.

blocks.title: Core mental model
blocks.content: A tool definition is an API contract: narrow purpose, precise schema, safe defaults, and actionable errors.
1. What Tool Definition Solves

Tool Definition belongs inside a wider AI system. It receives a defined input, performs one bounded responsibility, and produces an output that the next stage can validate. Keeping that boundary explicit prevents prompts, provider behavior, and business logic from becoming one fragile block.

["Define the user or system outcome before choosing Tool Definition.","Write down the input contract, output contract, latency target, and failure behavior.","Separate probabilistic model decisions from deterministic validation and side effects.","Keep provenance so outputs can be traced to inputs, model configuration, and tool results."]
items: Define the user or system outcome before choosing Tool Definition.
Write down the input contract, output contract, latency target, and failure behavior.
Separate probabilistic model decisions from deterministic validation and side effects.
Keep provenance so outputs can be traced to inputs, model configuration, and tool results.

blocks.content: 2. End-to-End Architecture
A production Tool Definition implementation is a pipeline. Each stage should be independently measurable and replaceable.

["Expose only tools allowed for this user and task.","Describe inputs with a strict schema.","Let the model propose a call.","Validate arguments and authorize the exact action.","Execute with idempotency, timeout, and audit logging.","Return a compact structured result to the model."]
items: Expose only tools allowed for this user and task.
Describe inputs with a strict schema.
Let the model propose a call.
Validate arguments and authorize the exact action.
Execute with idempotency, timeout, and audit logging.
Return a compact structured result to the model.

blocks.title: Boundary rule
blocks.content: Every external response and model-generated structure must be validated before it enters trusted application logic.

args = schema.validate(proposal.arguments)
policy.authorize(user, proposal.name, args)
result = executor.run(proposal.name, args,
                      idempotency_key=request_id, timeout=10)

blocks.content: The example keeps the orchestration small and pushes validation, policy, storage, and execution into explicit services. This makes unit tests possible and prevents a provider SDK from becoming the architecture.
4. Production Failure Modes

["Using Tool Definition without a measurable success criterion.","Allowing unbounded input, context, output, retries, or tool calls.","Assuming a valid JSON shape also means the action is authorized or correct.","Hiding provider errors behind generic retries until latency and cost explode.","Shipping without representative offline tests and production traces."]
items: Using Tool Definition without a measurable success criterion.
Allowing unbounded input, context, output, retries, or tool calls.
Assuming a valid JSON shape also means the action is authorized or correct.
Hiding provider errors behind generic retries until latency and cost explode.
Shipping without representative offline tests and production traces.

blocks.title: Least authority
blocks.content: Give the model the minimum context and the minimum set of capabilities required for the current request. Capability discovery must never silently become capability authorization.
6. When to Use It

7. Interview Checklist

["Explain Tool Definition in one sentence and name the problem it solves.","Draw the request flow and identify every trust boundary.","State the validation, authorization, timeout, retry, and fallback strategy.","Describe the offline evaluation set and the production metrics.","Discuss one quality, latency, cost, and security tradeoff.","Explain how the design changes at ten times the traffic or data volume."]
items: Explain Tool Definition in one sentence and name the problem it solves.
Draw the request flow and identify every trust boundary.
State the validation, authorization, timeout, retry, and fallback strategy.
Describe the offline evaluation set and the production metrics.
Discuss one quality, latency, cost, and security tradeoff.
Explain how the design changes at ten times the traffic or data volume.

blocks.content: Tool Definition is production-ready when its behavior is bounded, measurable, recoverable, and safe—not merely when the happy-path demo works.
